findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions on ec2, s3, lambda and cloudwatch against Resource "*" with no conditions. This violates least privilege and enables privilege escalation, for example launching EC2 instances with existing instance profiles or modifying Lambda function code and roles.

A permanent IAM access key is created for the user and no pgp_key is supplied, so the secret access key is stored unencrypted in Terraform state. Combined with the wildcard policy attached to this same user, exposure of state yields highly privileged, non-rotating credentials.

The IAM user has no permissions boundary and no MFA condition while holding a wildcard inline policy and a static access key, so a single leaked credential grants broad account access with no compensating control.
